name: eip681-conformance

parse(uri) ->.target: string|null  // address right after the scheme: the PAYEE for native, the TOKEN CONTRACT for /transfer
parse(uri) ->.chainId: number|null // null = absent. MUST NOT be defaulted to 1
parse(uri) ->.params: object // raw query params as strings
parse(uri) ->.recipient: string|null // for /transfer: the `address` param = the real payee
parse(uri) ->.amount: bigint|null // exact base units (wei, or token base units)

notes: Machine-readable conformance vectors for EIP-681 parsers.
Ground truth, in order: (A) the EIP-681 spec text, (B) official Keccak-256
vectors, (C) the four canonical EIP-55 checksum vectors.
INTENT: a wallet team should be able to drop this in and get a red/green
signal for the URI grammar without writing their own corpus.
CORRECTED 2026-09-23: 1.0.0 contained two vectors with the SAME uri and
opposite expectations (the 'mangled mixed case' fixture was written fully
lowercase, i.e. not mixed case at all). Also field names now match the
documented parser interface above. Found by running, not by reading.
The mixed-case pair (bad-mixedcase vs all-lowercase) is the highest-value
test here: identical bytes, opposite verdicts.

vectors.why: Bare `ethereum:ADDRESS`, no @chainId. VALID. Absent chainId means 'current chain' by convention -- it does NOT mean chain 1. Defaulting it to 1 silently converts a 'whatever chain' intent into a mainnet transfer.
`value` is in wei and MAY use scientific notation (1e16 = 0.01 ETH = 10000000000000000 wei). Parse as an exact decimal string / BigInt; Number() loses precision above 2^53 wei.
Scheme match MUST be case-insensitive. Capitalised scheme prefixes appear in the wild.

THE DANGEROUS CASE. The segment before `/transfer` is the TOKEN CONTRACT (0x8335...A02913 = USDC on Base). The payee is the `address` query param. A scanner that treats the post-`ethereum:` segment as the recipient sends funds to the token contract instead of the person. Wallets without function-call support fail by sending to the wrong place, not by erroring.

Canonical EIP-55 vector #2 is 0xfB6916095ca1df60bB79Ce92cE3Ea74c37c5d359. Here the leading `f` is uppercased, so the string is MIXED CASE -- an explicit EIP-55 claim -- and the claim fails. Still 40 hex chars, still the same 20 bytes. A lenient parser accepts it and pays the right address by luck; a strict one rejects it. Rejecting is correct: a corrupted casing is indistinguishable from a corrupted address. Contrast with the next vector: SAME BYTES, opposite verdict.
All-lowercase carries NO checksum claim, so it is valid and must be accepted. This is the same 20 bytes as the vector above; only the casing differs. Getting this pair right IS the test.
EIP-681's scheme is `ethereum:` with NO slashes. Parsers that split on a generic `://` will accept this and then mishandle the real `ethereum:` form. Strip the literal prefix, not a URL scheme.

`value` (native currency, wei) and `uint256` (ERC-20 call argument, token base units) must not both appear on the same target. Mixing them is unit confusion: the same number means two different things in two different currencies.
No target. Must be rejected, not treated as an empty address.
